content: {"summary":"fraud-scorer-02 was OOMKilled within minutes after each restart on 28 May 2026 because the Deployment did not set WEB_CONCURRENCY, so the pod started one gunicorn worker per CPU (32 workers on a 32‑core node). Each worker used ~150 MiB, so after about 20 workers the 3 GiB memory limit was reached, triggering OOM. Reducing the worker count to 16 by setting WEB_CONCURRENCY fixed the problem.","likely_cause":"Default gunicorn worker count matched node CPU cores (32) exceeding the pod memory limit, leading to rapid OOM kills.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"OOMKilled fast because WEB_CONCURRENCY was unset, causing 32 gunicorn workers to start","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#1"],"quote":"WEB_CONCURRENCY is not set in the Deployment, so the entrypoint starts one gunicorn worker per CPU it can see: 32"},{"text":"Each worker used ~150 MiB, so ~20 workers filled the 3 GiB limit, causing OOM after ~11 minutes","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#2"],"quote":"The kill came once about 20 workers had warmed up (3,072 / 150 ≈ 20)"},{"text":"Setting WEB_CONCURRENCY=16 reduced workers to 16 and stopped the OOM loop","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#2"],"quote":"WEB_CONCURRENCY=16 set in the Deployment; rollout 02:40 both pods running 16 workers"}],"next_checks":["Verify that WEB_CONCURRENCY remains set to 16 or appropriate value in the fraud‑scorer Deployment","Monitor memory usage after the change to ensure no further OOM events","Audit other Deployments that derive worker count from CPU cores for similar risk"]}
